en fremvisning.explanation: "En fremvisning" means "a showing / display". It comes from the verb "at fremvise" (to show). To say a home is shown to buyers, use "en visning" (a viewing) instead: "Vi har visning på lørdag" (We have a viewing on Saturday).

en fridag.explanation: "En fridag" means "a day off". It is built from "fri" (free) and "en dag" (a day). To say you are off today, use "fri" alone: "Jeg har fri i dag" (I am off today).

en frihed.explanation: "En frihed" means "a freedom". The word is the last part of "ytringsfrihed" (freedom of speech): "Der er ytringsfrihed i Danmark" (There is freedom of speech in Denmark).

en frikadelle.explanation: "En frikadelle" means "a meatball". In Denmark, it is a flat fried patty, eaten hot with potatoes or cold on rye bread.

en frist.explanation: "En frist" means "a deadline". To talk about meeting or extending a deadline, use these verbs: "at overholde en frist" (to meet a deadline) and "at forlænge en frist" (to extend a deadline).

en frisure.explanation: "En frisure" means "a hairstyle". Use it for the cut and the styling together. A haircut, "en klipning", is only the cutting: "Jeg har tid til en klipning" (I have an appointment for a haircut).

en frisør.explanation: "En frisør" means "a hairdresser". It also means the place where you get a haircut: "Jeg har tid hos frisøren" (I have an appointment at the hairdresser's).

en frisørsalon.explanation: "En frisørsalon" means "a hair salon". It is built from "frisør" (hairdresser) and "en salon" (a salon). To book a visit, use "at bestille tid" (to book an appointment): "Jeg har bestilt tid til torsdag" (I have booked an appointment for Thursday).

en fritidsaktivitet.explanation: "En fritidsaktivitet" means "a leisure activity". It is built from "fritid" (free time) and "en aktivitet" (an activity). To ask what someone does in their free time, say: "Hvad laver du i din fritid?" (What do you do in your free time?)

en fritidsordning.explanation: "En fritidsordning" means "an after-school program". It is built from "fritid" (free time) and "en ordning" (an arrangement). In Denmark, the best-known kind is "SFO" (short for "skolefritidsordning"), for the youngest school children: "Min søn er i SFO" (My son is in SFO).

en frivillig.explanation: "En frivillig" means "a volunteer". To say something is not required, use the adjective: "Det er frivilligt" (It is voluntary).

en frokostpause.explanation: "En frokostpause" means "a lunch break". It is built from "frokost" (lunch) and "en pause" (a break). To say someone is on their lunch break, use "i" (in): "Hun er i frokostpause" (She is on her lunch break).

en front.explanation: "En front" means "a front". When you talk about war, it means the line where two armies fight: "Soldaterne er ved fronten" (The soldiers are at the front).

en frugt.explanation: "En frugt" means "a fruit". When you talk about fruit as food in general, say "frugt" without an article: "Jeg spiser meget frugt" (I eat a lot of fruit). To count single pieces, use "et stykke frugt" (a piece of fruit): "Jeg tager et stykke frugt" (I will take a piece of fruit).

en frugthave.explanation: "En frugthave" means "an orchard". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en have" (a garden). Do not mix up the verb "at have" (to have) and "en have" (a garden): "Vi har en have" (We have a garden).

en frugtplantage.explanation: "En frugtplantage" means "an orchard". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en plantage" (a plantation). To say you pick fruit there, use "at plukke" (to pick): "Vi plukker kirsebær i frugtplantagen" (We pick cherries in the orchard).

en frugtsalat.explanation: "En frugtsalat" means "a fruit salad". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en salat" (a salad). To say you have it as the last course, use "til dessert" (for dessert): "Vi får frugtsalat til dessert" (We are having fruit salad for dessert).

en frugtskål.explanation: "En frugtskål" means "a fruit bowl". It is built from "frugt" (fruit) and "en skål" (a bowl). The word "skål" is also what you say when you raise a glass: "Skål!" (Cheers!)

en frustration.explanation: "En frustration" means "a frustration". It is related to the adjective "frustreret" (frustrated): "Jeg er frustreret over trafikken" (I am frustrated about the traffic).

en frysepose.explanation: "En frysepose" means "a freezer bag". It is built from "at fryse" (to freeze) and "en pose" (a bag). To describe food that is in the freezer, use "frossen" (frozen): "frossen fisk" (frozen fish).

en fryser.explanation: "En fryser" means "a freezer". Do not mix it up with the verb "at fryse" (to be cold): "Jeg fryser" (I am cold). "En fryser" is the appliance: "Der er is i fryseren" (There is ice cream in the freezer).

en frø.explanation: "En frø" means "a frog". It takes "en", as the form "frøen" shows. Do not mix it up with "et frø" (a seed): "Jeg lægger et frø i jorden" (I put a seed in the soil).

en frøken.explanation: "En frøken" means "a miss / young lady". To use it as a title before a last name, write: "frøken Hansen" (Miss Hansen).

en frøpose.explanation: "En frøpose" means "a seed packet". It is built from "et frø" (a seed) and "en pose" (a bag). Do not mix up "et frø" (a seed) with "en frø" (a frog). "Et frø": "Jeg lægger et frø i jorden" (I put a seed in the soil). "En frø": "En frø sidder ved søen" (A frog sits by the lake).

en fugl.explanation: "En fugl" means "a bird". The word "fugl" is also part of "en fuglekasse" (a birdhouse): "Vi har sat en fuglekasse op" (We have put up a birdhouse).
